trace.query: SELECT id, page, text FROM lines WHERE text ILIKE '%limonene%' OR text ILIKE '%nerolidol%' ORDER BY page, line_no

rendered:
Limonene and nerolidol titers appear in the Introduction, in the section headed "Production of other heterologous compounds[1]", and in Table 2[2].

Introduction, nerolidol maximum titer: "70.50[3]" g/L.
Section on other heterologous compounds, nerolidol: "(E)-Nerolidol reached 70.50[4]" g/L, citing "[24][5]".
The table, nerolidol: "70,500[6]" mg/L, over "96[7]" h, fed-batch, reference "[24][8]". The nerolidol value agrees across the Introduction, the section headed as above, and the table once units are converted from mg/L to g/L.

Section on other heterologous compounds, limonene: "limonene reached 22.8[9]" g/L, described as the highest reported value and citing reference "[21][10]".
The table, limonene: "22,800[11]" mg/L, over "100[12]" h, fed-batch, reference "[21][13]". The limonene value agrees between the section and the table once units are converted.

Bioreactor values: the section headed as above also describes a shake-flask study of various terpenoids, attributed to "Wang et al.[14]" citing "[16][15]": limonene "14.12[16]" g/L and nerolidol "32.33[17]" g/L "in 5-L bioreactors[18]".

Consistency issues: the bioreactor values are not in the table. The table rows that cite the same reference are for isoprenol[19] and isoprene[20], not limonene or nerolidol, so the table does not support the attribution of these values to that reference. The lower limonene and nerolidol bioreactor values are also not reconciled with the literature maxima stated elsewhere in the paper. They are not contradicted, since they could come from different strains or conditions, but the text does not say so.

The outlook also names limonene and nerolidol as products: "high-value terpenoids (e.g., (S)-limonene and nerolidol)[21]".
